title: Capacity experimentation calendar and canary criteria for dedicated autoscale
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Objective: Produce a quarter-long experimentation calendar and a minimal, actionable canary criteria set to validate predictive warm-pool and surge-autoscale strategies for Dedicated capacity. Scope: define 6 experiments (3 predictive warm-pool variants, 2 surge orchestration policies, 1 fallback orchestration), success metrics, rollout gates, monitoring dashboards, and operational runbooks. Deliverables: experiment calendar (dates + cohorts), canary pass/fail checklist, telemetry dashboard queries, example rollout manifests, incident rollback playbook, and an outcomes decision rubric for capacity commitments. Motivation: teams need a repeatable way to test adaptive autoscale policies against real traffic patterns without risking SLAs or overspending reserved pools. This ticket coordinates PM, Eng, SRE, and Finance to align on measurable decision thresholds for Q2 capacity commitments.
acceptance_criteria: A calendar with weekly experiment windows and assigned owners published to Confluence
A canary checklist with concrete pass/fail thresholds (latency P95, 1min error rate, cost delta) that SRE and Eng sign off on
Dashboard queries and alerts implemented (token-level cost, prewarm hit-rate, queue latency) and linked from the doc
Two pilot experiments complete in staging with documented outcomes and a recommended policy to trial in a single dedicated pool
Runbook and rollback steps created and validated in a tabletop exercise with oncall engineers
decisions: Use predictive warm pools + minimum burst buffer (30% capacity) as the primary experiment axis
Experiment windows set to 72-hour active ingestion per cohort to capture diurnal patterns
Canary pass criteria: P95 latency regression <= 10% vs baseline, 1min error rate < 0.5%, estimated cost delta <= 15% for improved latency
If canary fails, fallback to static pool sizing and abort capacity commitment changes for that cohort
next_steps: Finalize Confluence experiment calendar and assign owners (due 2026-01-15)
Eng implements experimental policy hooks (ENG-2410) and adds feature flags for warm-pool variants
SRE to author dashboard queries and add alerting for canary channels
Schedule tabletop runbook rehearsal with oncall and ops (target 2026-02-05)

notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive prewarm improves latency but risks unnecessary reserved time; canary windows need to be long enough to capture diurnal effects but short enough to avoid extended exposure.
Risk mitigations: small cohorts, explicit cost gates, automated rollback flag, and tabletop rehearsals before production rollout.
